History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old woman with a 3-day history of worsening right-sided predominantly peri-orbital headache with photophobia and nausea, unrelieved by low-dose ibuprofen; clinical impression is migraine-type headache. Management discussed: maximize NSAID dose or start naproxen ± paracetamol/codeine, keep headache diary, follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if red-flag symptoms.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Headache.  
• Onset: Began ~3 days ago while at work.  
• Course: Persistent with episodic exacerbations; overall worsening over 3 days.  
• Location: Diffuse but mainly around right eye.  
• Character/severity: Dull baseline with intermittent sharper pain, rated 8/10 at worst.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: Bright light aggravates (photophobia). Ibuprofen 3 tabs/day for 2 days provided no relief (previous headaches usually relieved by ibuprofen). No other specific triggers identified.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (“shooting lights”), nausea (“feel sick”) without vomiting, difficulty concentrating.  
• Pertinent negatives: No blurred or lost vision, no neck stiffness, no speech or motor deficits, no fever, no rash, no recent head trauma.  
• Relevant ROS: No other systemic symptoms reported.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior diagnosis of migraine; has had occasional headaches in past responsive to ibuprofen.

Medications:
• Ibuprofen – self-administered, 3 tablets/day for 2 days; dose/route/frequency detail not documented (likely sub-therapeutic).  
• No regular prescription medications.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with three housemates.  
• Occupation: IT work; prolonged computer use.  
• Tobacco: Social smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social drinker.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.  
• Reports mild workplace stress due to new project.  
• Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye examination.

Family History:
• Mother – frequent migraines (seasonal).  
• Sister – occasional migraines.  
• No other familial illnesses discussed.

Physical Examination:
No examination findings or vitals documented in transcript.

Investigations:
None performed or reviewed during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected migraine-type headache
  • Assessment: 3-day escalating periorbital headache with photophobia, nausea, positive family history; refractory to current NSAID dose. No red-flag features elicited.
  • Plan: 
    – Counsel on appropriate ibuprofen dosing (up to 400 mg two tablets TID with food) OR prescribe naproxen if preferred.  
    – Consider adding paracetamol and/or codeine for additional analgesia.  
    – Advise keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.  
    – Educate on hydration, regular meals, screen brightness adjustment, stress reduction.  
    – Re-evaluate in 1–2 weeks; earlier review if worsening, visual changes, focal neurologic deficits, vomiting, fever, or other concerning symptoms.  
    – Discuss possibility of prophylactic therapy at follow-up if headaches become frequent.

General Plan items:
• Recommend routine eye examination due to prolonged computer work and visual strain.
• Encourage smoking cessation and moderation of alcohol.

Quality checks:

Missing but clinically expected elements:
• Complete physical examination and vital signs not documented.
• Detailed medication reconciliation (OTC, supplements) incomplete.
• Exact ibuprofen dosage (mg/tablet) not specified.
Internal conflicts:
• None noted.
Transcript quality:
• Clear overall; occasional minor pauses/fillers, no inaudible sections.
